boards.title: Your First Weekend at Scripps College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend loop through Scripps’ named gardens, art, history, and shared campus spaces.

cards.title: Start at Honnold Gate
cards.subtitle: A campus-map-listed entrance to Scripps
cards.notes: Use the gate as a clear first landmark, then follow the campus map toward the central courts and gardens at an unhurried pace.
cards.short_summary: Begin with a named campus entrance and orient yourself to the grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps’ campus map lists Honnold Gate as a campus location.
cards.access_notes: Use exterior walkways and follow posted campus access guidance.

cards.title: Walk Olive Walk
cards.subtitle: Named Scripps campus view
cards.notes: Make Olive Walk an early outdoor pause: look for the named route in the College’s campus imagery and continue toward nearby historic spaces.
cards.short_summary: A simple outdoor leg through a named campus landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps includes Olive Walk among its official campus-view images.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor viewing only; follow any posted access guidance.

cards.title: Find Denison Library
cards.subtitle: Campus-map-listed library and special-collections repository
cards.notes: Pause outside to locate Denison’s distinctive building, then save an interior collections visit for an appointment or its published open hours.
cards.short_summary: Get your bearings at Scripps’ historic library before planning a return visit.
cards.evidence_claim: Denison Library is Scripps’ repository for special collections and archives; its summer 2026 access is by appointment.
cards.access_notes: Summer 2026: appointment Monday–Friday through August 28; do not assume weekend interior access.

cards.title: Enter Margaret Fowler Garden
cards.subtitle: Historic cloister garden at the center of campus
cards.notes: Take a quiet lap through the garden and use the fountain, arbor, and surrounding architecture as cues to slow the first-day campus tour.
cards.short_summary: A named garden stop that combines campus landscaping and historic architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps describes Margaret Fowler Garden as a medieval-style cloister garden with a chapel, wisteria, and a historical mural.
cards.source_title: A Public Art Tour of The Claremont Colleges
cards.access_notes: Outdoor viewing; do not pick flowers in this garden.

cards.title: Look Closely at The Flower Vendors
cards.subtitle: Alfredo Ramos Martinez mural in Margaret Fowler Garden
cards.notes: At the garden’s mural, take time to trace its long composition from a respectful distance and note the figures and color before moving on.
cards.short_summary: A focused art stop within the garden, centered on a documented 1946 mural.
cards.evidence_claim: The Flower Vendors is a 100-foot-long 1946 mural by Alfredo Ramos Martinez in Margaret Fowler Garden.
cards.source_title: A Public Art Tour of The Claremont Colleges
cards.access_notes: View the mural without touching it or surrounding plantings.

cards.title: Stroll the Rose Garden
cards.subtitle: Historic garden beside Graffiti Wall
cards.notes: Continue to the Rose Garden for an outdoor reset, then use its location beside Graffiti Wall to connect landscape and class history.
cards.short_summary: A short garden walk that leads naturally to a central Scripps tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps’ 1930 timeline says the Rose Garden was planted for students and later restored with roses from the original plan.
cards.access_notes: Enjoy the garden from public walkways and follow current campus rules for any flower cutting.

cards.title: Read Graffiti Wall
cards.subtitle: Between Toll Hall and Browning Hall
cards.notes: Read the class imagery as an outdoor history display; leave the wall unchanged, since Scripps assigns the signing and mural-making role to seniors.
cards.short_summary: See the visual record created by Scripps graduating classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps says Graffiti Wall is between Toll and Browning and gives each graduating class a place to create an image and sign names.
cards.access_notes: Viewing is appropriate; only the senior class participates in its signing tradition.

cards.title: Visit the Scripps Student Garden
cards.subtitle: Behind Browning Hall
cards.notes: Walk through the garden’s paths and notice the planting beds, fruit trees, murals, and study areas; check with coordinators before joining work or harvests.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor sustainability stop with documented student-led programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Scripps Student Garden, behind Browning, has seasonal fruit trees, planting beds, murals, and study areas.
cards.access_notes: Respect active garden work and ask before harvesting or participating in a program.

cards.title: Find Swing Low: Harriet Tubman Memorial
cards.subtitle: Sculpture garden at Bixby Court
cards.notes: Finish the art walk at Bixby Court by viewing Alison Saar’s sculpture and using the nearby gallery courtyard as a final campus landmark.
cards.short_summary: A documented sculpture-garden stop near the Williamson Gallery.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps identifies Swing Low: Harriet Tubman Memorial, 2007, by alumna Alison Saar in the sculpture garden surrounding Bixby Court.
cards.source_title: Scripps College Dedicates Sculpture of Harriet Tubman for New Sculpture Garden
cards.access_notes: Outdoor sculpture viewing; do not climb or touch the artwork.

cards.title: End with the Williamson Gallery
cards.subtitle: 251 East 11th Street, on the Scripps campus
cards.notes: If an exhibition is on view, step inside for the final stop; otherwise use the courtyard to mark the end of the first-weekend campus loop.
cards.short_summary: A free public gallery visit when an exhibition is open.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ruth Chandler Williamson Gallery is free and open to the public during exhibitions, Wednesday through Sunday from noon to 5 PM.
cards.access_notes: Interior access is only during exhibitions, Wednesday–Sunday, 12–5 PM; confirm an exhibition date before going.
